_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 9 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_status: Version 71 is live (S275, 2026-09-18 08:26Z). When someone says which credential they hold and asks what it could count toward, the first course Sierra names is now in the program they want to enter; the courses of the program that trains what they already hold come last, marked as background, because the credential record matches both credentials and only the visitor's own words say which one is held. Every retrieval lookup now has its own five-second limit (tunable without a deploy), and its first cut was measured and harmless. The A/B compare's verdict now fails the job when it reads a regression (it never had). Open for Sam: read version 71's Orange County answer; which Orange County college runs LVN entry training; the 381 garbled course rows; auto-deploy on merge; the scope of guidance rule 674923db. Version 71's first production answer attached a Mt. San Antonio course to Golden West College, so the next build puts the college on every course line and the Chaffey precedent inside the block, beside the courses it is evidence for.  In parallel, SkyView became shareable: it states on its face that it is read only and where curation is saved, a drag that merges nothing now answers instead of going quiet, and a merged course queues in line against its parent circle awaiting a curator. Its served page is generated, and a guard now compares it to its sources so a hand-edit cannot ship again.

items.text: Put a PreToolUse hook in front of mcp__Supabase__execute_sql once Sam picks it. #1617 allowlisted five Supabase tools; four are read-only by construction, and execute_sql runs arbitrary SQL against the project holding map_student_credit (537,908 student-grain rows), kb_curation (32,441) and team_access. Rule 10's write discipline is doctrine and the permission prompt was its only mechanism. The hook passes reads and blocks INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, DROP and ALTER, so the Sierra lane keeps frictionless exploratory reads. Say the limit plainly in the hook's own comment: a pattern over SQL is a guardrail against accident, not a security boundary — a CTE carrying an INSERT, a DO block or a function with side effects can pass naive matching. The stronger alternative, if Sam prefers it, is a Postgres role with no write grants, where the database enforces it and no pattern is needed.

ANSWERED 2026-09-18 — you said yes to SkyView saving a merge itself, and asked that the build happen in the next session. Two calls are still yours. The RE-MINT SHAPE: a corpus re-key is a batch migration and cannot come from a browser (the playbook needs producer and consumer in one git commit plus a gated Supabase re-key inside a window closing before the 10:17 UTC cron), but a principled re-mint of specific identities is expressible as a request — SkyView composes it, shows the dry-run's blast radius on the map, takes your approval, and a dispatched workflow lands it. Smallest first step is that blast-radius view alone, read only, no approve button. The EXECUTE_SQL GUARD: the allowlist from #1617 removed the prompt that was the only thing enforcing Rule 10's write discipline on a database holding 537,908 student-grain rows; recommended fix is a PreToolUse hook that passes reads and blocks write verbs, which keeps the speed Sierra needs. Both are written up in cpl_memory.

BUILD IT — Sam said yes on 2026-09-18. The cpl_session.js sign-in keeper (31 modules already read a reviewer session), a Save control on the staged list, the same kb_curation merge_into POST unified_courses.js makes, the undo that already exists as a row delete, and one entry in kb/governance_surface_map.json with its reason, because a read-only surface gaining writes is a decision-rights change under Rule 10 (a3). Two things the yes carries that are easy to miss. tests/ccr_skyview_read_only.test.js asserts the page has exactly one non-GET request and no rest/v1 call at all — that guard was written to resist a casual change, so update it deliberately rather than route around it. And the band's sentence stops being true for one audience: 'Moves stage in this browser alone' is false for a signed-in curator and still true for everyone else, including the people Sam is sharing the page with, whose writes RLS refuses. Make the band conditional on session state and keep the non-reviewer's version accurate — he shared the page on that sentence.

Decide whether to re-order SkyView's hit test for the one-in-twenty-four eclipse. Measured 2026-09-18 over eight parent identities through the page's own pick(): 23 of 24 loners resolve to themselves with their parent open, and 37 of 37 focused member stars resolve to that member. The reading rule is perfect, so chasing the 1 risks the 37 and pick() was left unchanged; with the silent drop exit fixed, that case now reads as a clear refusal rather than a dead map. Reopen it only if Sam hits it again.

Put the college on every course line and the CNA-to-LVN precedent inside the prospective block. Version 71's first production answer opened 'At Golden West College, ask … to review your CNA certificate against VOC VN1 / Vocational Nursing 1' — that course is Mt. San Antonio's, and Golden West teaches no LVN course: the block lists courses under a college heading with no college on the line, and the model re-attached a course to the county's college. Three of the last four answers also said no college had articulated a CNA credential against an LVN course while the credential record carried Chaffey's NURVN 414. Render each course line with its college, compute the precedent line for the held titles and render it under the target program's heading, say in the rule that college and course come from the same heading, and pin both; the smoke fails when an Orange County college name precedes an LVN course code in the first 300 characters.

Measure the program search's latency under the smoke's load. The route time limit cut it once in the version 71 A/B (5,002 ms on the Boys & Girls Club question) and the answer failed safe with no program catalog; the route usually answers in one to three seconds. Read the function logs for every cut line over a week, then decide whether the query moves or the limit does. Never an index on the programs table (#1602).

Say go on deleting 381 garbled course-title rows. Sierra's course lists showed Pasadena's NURS 102 as 'Fundamentals of Vocational Nursing Ã¢â‚¬â€œ Theory'. The loaders are fixed so the next nightly sync writes clean titles, but the course table's sync only adds and never deletes, and its match key includes the title, so the 381 garbled rows (84 colleges) would sit beside the repaired ones and double the alignment candidates. The plan: after the first clean sync, delete rows whose title carries the garbled sequences, with a receipt listing each row so it can be put back. A shared-table write, so it waits for your go.

Make the course-catalog replace atomic. The offerings sync truncates on its first chunk and appends the rest, each chunk its own transaction, so a chunk the database cancels leaves a partial catalog live. It happened twice on 18 September (12,000 then 8,000 of 16,097 rows) and Sierra answered from the partial catalog for forty minutes. Smaller chunks with a retry are in; the real fix loads into a staging table and swaps in one statement. Until then, expect any merge that edits a loader to re-sync the catalog beside its own smoke run.

Read Sierra's new program answers in a browser. She is live (version 67) with the third view of a college — the degrees and certificates it awards — and every check we can run passed, but no human has read the prose yet. Try 'Where can I train to become an LVN?', 'Which colleges award a welding certificate?', and one question that names your home college. Odd answers are expected and welcome: each one becomes a fixture or a vocabulary entry, the way the negation class is handled.

Decide whether the assistant should deploy itself when we merge. Today its page goes live on merge and the function behind it waits for someone to push a button — the same gap that left Sierra dark for five days in September while every check said she was fine. Making it automatic removes that gap and also removes a human pause before a change reaches students. Our recommendation is to make it automatic and keep the button for undoing.

Open My College signed out and tell us it reads right. A college with withheld rows should show a 'Withheld to protect small student counts' line inside the breakdown, and the contacts list should say which roles are staff-only rather than calling them blank. Our automated check cannot load this page's data, so your eyes are the check.

Name the Orange County college that runs LVN ENTRY training, if one does. You called 'no OC colleges have LVN' flat wrong (2026-09-18); the COCI extract lists only the LVN-to-RN bridges at Cypress, Golden West and Saddleback, and no course under the Vocational Nursing TOP in the county, so Sierra now says what the catalog shows and names the bridges. If entry training exists and the extract misses it, that is a data gap to trace in the loader.

Work out why Sierra's uptime check runs about four times a day when it is scheduled eight times. Observed across three days, not yet diagnosed. The gap between checks is how long an outage can sit unnoticed.

Version 71 is live (2026-09-18, 08:26Z). Ask the Orange County question again in a browser. The first sentence now names the course to ask about in the LVN program (Long Beach City's VN 220, Rio Hondo's VN 61, Mt. San Antonio's VOC VN101); the CNA program's own courses come last, marked as background; the catalog absence is stated as the catalog's with the three bridges named; no answer opens with a remark about the question. The Chaffey precedent is cited in about one answer in four, so the next build puts it in the block. Tell us whether it now reads right.

Decide whether to re-scope the team guidance rule that says 'answer with the colleges that have ALREADY articulated it, first and plainly'. The assistant's prompt let it govern a different question (what might my credential count toward), which is why version 69 led with an exhibit table. Version 70 scopes it in code; editing the rule itself in the Training tab to open with 'When someone asks where a credential ALREADY earns credit' would make the scope visible to the team.

For a question that names a college, order the nearby lists by distance alone. Today the county band still comes first, so from Long Beach City College an Antelope Valley program 110 miles away outranks Cypress 12 miles away across the county line. A named place keeps its band; a named college should not.

Verify the 119 campus coordinates against IPEDS from a machine that can reach nces.ed.gov (the sandbox cannot). They were entered from public campus locations to about a mile; a wrong point changes which college leads a list.

_deferred.text: Reconcile two readings of one manual. The state's Taxonomy of Programs marks career-education programs with an asterisk, and the copy in the program export disagrees with the copy we parsed ourselves on 495 of 20,727 programs. Neither is obviously right. Until it is settled we read the marker for display only and never as a fact about a program.

One of our search files points at a test file that has never existed. The exhibit search names chatbox/verify_search_exhibits_v2.sql as the thing that proves it works, and git shows it was never written or deleted. Either write it or remove the claim — a pointer to nothing is worse than no pointer.

Send the Academic Senate (ASCCC) area roster — which college sits in which area. Every Supabase column matching area, senate, asccc, zone or region was searched and none carries them. Strong Workforce regions are already solved.

The occupation matcher's misses are a VOCABULARY problem, not a tuning one. Application developer and Computer Programming share no word, so no threshold reaches them. The register is live in the My College tab and discloses the gap, so this is about making it find more rather than about shipping. Closing it needs a synonym layer or the curated occupation map — and two plausible shortcuts are already measured and rejected in the code.

Decide whether the Common Exhibit Reference should canonicalize against the credential registry — adopting the issuer's own credential name and the issuing agency in place of a vote among the freehand titles colleges typed.

When the origination data lands, half of it works by itself and half does not. The noncredit location side switches on automatically. The landing page / portal / batch upload side waits for a deliberate one-line change, made only once the exact spellings are confirmed, and the only signal that it is waiting is a line in a daily log. Worth giving that to someone by name.

Add the 369 California licenses to the college handout as a third column, beside the exhibits a college can adopt and the ones it could build. The handout already carries the accuracy caveat, so the new column needs the same treatment: say what is confirmed and what a person in the room should check.

One thing from the 15 September decision sheet is yours: a note to MAP about the Dashboard's "Eligible" label, which actually shows applied credit. It is drafted and waiting for you to send at docs/map_eligible_label_note_draft.md — check the figures again first, because the reconciliation is the whole argument.

After Sam's deploy, read the new log columns: how many turns came from a signed-in reviewer, how many from the team phrase, how many from the public, and from which surface. The count of six real questions in thirty hours could not tell the COBI tabs from the public page; now it can. Also show those two columns in Sierra Training's conversation list, which reads the same table.

Build the floating assistant bubble on every COBI tab — Sam's ask from the 11th. The flag it needed exists now; the control does not. It mounts the same assistant the CPL Assistant tab uses, in the house style, with controls at least 24 pixels tall and a single column on a phone. What a signed-in reader may additionally see is a separate decision that goes through Governance first.

The health probe asks one simple question, so it cannot see the failure where Sierra answers broad questions with silence — it passed straight through two hours of that on the 11th. Rather than pay for a second question every run, have the probe read how many blank answers the live table recorded since its last run. That costs nothing and watches real visitors instead of its own test question.

Forward the KYND memo (vault: 20260911_Memo_map_rccd_edu_WordPress_wp2shell_Notice.docx) to whoever holds the SiteGround login for map.rccd.edu, filling in the TO line. Two things come back: the WordPress version on both the production site and staging2.map.rccd.edu, which the notice did not list, and whether the log search found anything. Then answer KYND. Until the site is confirmed clean, the Monday job that copies the site's story cards onto the Fact Sheet keeps running; pausing it is your call, and the current cards checked clean.

What is left behind the assistant after Sam's two rulings of the 11th. The sixteen-row register sweep on Sonnet 5 with reasoning off has still not been run — it is the hardest thing she does and the one caller with no record yet, and it now matters more than it did: the check for whether her answers are being cut short came back clean, but almost nobody is using her yet (six real questions in thirty hours against four hundred and forty of our own), so watching live traffic mostly watches ourselves. The sweep is the only test that would really exercise the new, much higher answer limit. After it, an A/B of private reasoning at low effort on the preview copy, but only if the sweep shows a gap — Sam's words were "test for better options if they exist."

Eleven decisions from the sheet of the 11th are settled and waiting to be built. Two carry an instruction rather than a plain yes: every panel tint becomes the one pale gray rather than six near-identical shades, and Pierce College keeps the Los Angeles in its name — the bare spelling was a mistake, not a variant to support. The rest: a permanent name beside each statewide credential, five refinements to the CPL view, the twenty-four places asking for a colour that was never defined, the faint grey notes on the Implementation Funding tab, splitting the explainer footer so sources can be hidden, the published standard to start from, the phrase people type before moving a course, and letting an assistant instruction apply only to SkyView questions.

Six observations from the full sweep of SkyView are still open for your read. You have already ruled on one of them: the check boxes stay for now, because people cannot know what is available unless the list is in front of them. The rest are waiting.

Two follow-ups behind the CPL view. Ask SkyView on the CPL map still asks the assistant in course words (the discipline list is shared; the terms are course titles), so a question about credentials lands on discipline chips at best — the envelope needs a credential vocabulary. And the Courses map's Articulations light and the CPL map read the same record through opposite joins; a one-file test that they name the same pairs would catch the day one build drifts.

The statewide course descriptions you want a C-ID course to inherit are not in our data. You thought they came with the TMC tab work — that work gave us the 293 C-ID codes, which is probably what you are remembering, but not a word of the descriptive text behind them. So the ask to ASCCC is narrower than it looked: we have the identifiers and need only the descriptor prose.

Three things behind the daily dashboard, all data rather than display. The history file stops at 7 September because the build did not run for three days, and the gap has to be filled or the one-day comparison silently reads from the wrong date. The builder finds MAP's columns by name but falls back to a guessed position when a name moves, which is how it would produce confident wrong numbers rather than failing. And the moment MAP restores the CPL lifecycle checks, the counsellor-verified column goes back into the daily fetch.

What is left of the theme work, in one place. The faults still outstanding are dark greys sitting on dark backgrounds and a handful of pale backgrounds that never flipped, each individually named by the accessibility sweep. There is also a genuine bug found during that work which is wrong in both themes, not just the dark one: an unresolved brand link renders its own placeholder text. And a note for whoever picks this up — the probe that finds missing colour names reports what it fixed but not how many it found, so a run that finds nothing looks the same as a run that finds everything.

Sam's rule that expended and allocated are not interchangeable — colleges spend, the Chancellor's Office allocates — was applied at the one place it was found in the memo builder. The rest of the memo and report text has not been read against it. Check who the subject is in each sentence before changing either word; a blanket sweep would get it backwards.

Several of our own tests cannot fail. Seven files print no readable count of what they checked, so if their checks quietly vanished nobody would notice; and a test guarding a phrase that was later deleted kept passing while measuring nothing at all. This run added a third example and a habit that catches it: run a new test against the code as it was BEFORE the fix, and confirm it fails there.

DR-24 is a governance row with an owner and no surface yet: an added skill lands as proposed with the reviewer's name and the day, and joins the published outline when a second curator agrees; a removal works the same way in reverse. Building that means the map's first write, so it routes through Governance and the privacy review first.

Two housekeeping items behind the CPL face. Fifty-five exhibits in the articulation crosswalk are no longer in today's MAP feed; they stay on the map flagged in words rather than dropped, and the fix is a re-seed of the crosswalk from a fresh custom report. And the credit-funnel numbers the face carries for context were read by hand on 2026-09-07; refresh them after the next custom-report load.
